Hi Jane — great to meet you on the call. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Recap / recommended approach:
- Suggested models: redwood-7b-quant (best latency + cost for high throughput, recommended if your per-request sequences stay <=512 tokens) and redwood-13b-quant (better accuracy on edge cases, slightly higher p95 latency). For initial evals we usually run both in parallel and compare precision/recall on your prompt set.
- Prompt set: attached redwood_prompt_set_v1.json (includes canonical prompts, negative cases, and schema-expectation examples).
- Structured output schema: we suggest you use strict JSON Schema v4 with an optional top-level "errors" array. Examples are in the Drive benchmark folder. For evals we run both schema-compliance checks and fuzzy-matching on key fields to capture minor formatting differences.
- Function calling / retries: Redwood supports two patterns:
  1) Model-as-tool: model returns JSON conforming to schema; if parsing fails we surface the raw output plus a parsed-attempt and automatically retry up to 2 times with a sanitized prompt (strip ambiguous tokens).
  2) Deterministic extractor: use a small local deterministic post-processor for critical fields (recommended for billing IDs).
We will enable token-level traces and a webhook for any schema failures so you can alert and inspect.

Benchmarks & links:
- Drive folder with benchmark runs and p50/p95 numbers: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-benchmarks
- Eval harness for your samples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals-harness/tree/main/acme

Next steps / ask list:
- I will spin up a temporary eval workspace and invite your team (read-only) with 5k credits so you can run the two models against your sample set.
- Technical follow-up: Marissa (SE) and Aditya (Applied ML) to join a 45m deep-dive to discuss schema edge cases and instrumentation. Proposed times: Thu 03/05 09:00 PT or Fri 03/06 10:00 PT — which works?
- We will include an initial pricing estimate for a short POC (attached). If you need a Dedicated pool estimate we can provide that in the same doc.

Jane / Mike — looping Mike in. Short answers here and we'll cover in depth on Thursday: 

- Regression frequency: In our internal evals we see schema compliance failures ~2-4x higher on 7B-quant vs 13B-quant for complex multi-field outputs, but the delta reduces when you use tighter prompts and explicit JSON wrappers (we include examples in redwood_prompt_set_v1.json). For many customers the 7B-quant is acceptable if you add a deterministic post-check on critical fields.
- Retry patterns: we recommend 1 automated retry with a sanitized prompt that enforces the schema and then fallback to deterministic extraction for any remaining failures. Webhook + token traces are included in the eval workspace so you can instrument alerts off schema-failure events.
- Workspace & access: I'll invite both you and Mike to the temporary workspace by EOD (read-only + eval credits).

Also attaching a short pricing_estimate_acme.pdf with hosted POC numbers and a baseline Dedicated ballpark. If you'd like a formal SOW for Dedicated we can draft one after the POC.

See you Thu 03/05 09:00 PT — calendar invite sent by Marissa.

Best,
Rishi
